title: College Savings Strategies and 529 Education Plans
content:
With higher education costs consistently rising faster than general inflation, proactive college funding strategies are vital for families. In the United States, the primary vehicle for education savings is the 529 College Savings Plan.

A 529 plan is a state-sponsored, tax-advantaged investment account designed specifically for educational expenses. Similar to a Roth IRA, contributions are made with after-tax dollars, but investment earnings compound 100% free of federal and state income taxes. Withdrawals remain completely tax-free as long as the funds are spent on qualified educational expenses, including college tuition, fees, books, computers, and room and board.

Many individual states also offer state income tax deductions or credits for contributions made to their specific state plans. Furthermore, the SECURE 2.0 Act introduced a powerful provision: up to $35,000 in unused 529 funds can be rolled over tax-free into a Roth IRA in the beneficiary's name, eliminating fears that unused funds will be trapped or penalized.

When managing a 529 plan, many parents utilize age-based portfolios. These portfolios automatically adjust their asset allocation as the child grows—starting with 90% equities in early childhood for aggressive growth, and shifting predominantly into cash and fixed income as the child reaches high school.
